greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἥμαρτεν ὁ ἀρχιοινοχόος τοῦ βασιλέως Αἰγύπτου καὶ ὁ ἀρχισιτοποιὸς τῷ κυρίῳ αὐτῶν βασιλεῖ Αἰγύπτου.
hint: Pharaoh's chief cup-bearer and chief baker offend their master, the king of Egypt.

notes.text: ἁμαρτάνω, to miss the mark, err, sin, in the singular, with two subjects after it. The Hebrew has the plural, ḥāṭĕʾû.
Chief cup-bearer and chief baker: LSJ's glosses, each citing this chapter; Middle Liddell has neither compound.
ἐγένετο with no καί before the next verb: it came to be, after these things, the cup-bearer sinned.

names.gloss: (Αἴγυπτος, the Greek name of the land; Hebrew Miṣrayim)

greek: καὶ ὠργίσθη Φαραω ἐπὶ τοῖς δυσὶν εὐνούχοις αὐτοῦ, ἐπὶ τῷ ἀρχιοινοχόῳ καὶ ἐπὶ τῷ ἀρχισιτοποιῷ,
hint: Pharaoh is angry with his two eunuchs, the cup-bearer and the baker.

notes.text: The aorist passive of ὀργίζω, to make angry: he was made angry, with ἐπί and the dative of those he was angry at.
εὐνοῦχος, a eunuch, the title of 39:1, here of both men.

names.gloss: (Φαραω, from Hebrew Parʿōh, from the Egyptian for "great house")

greek: καὶ ἔθετο αὐτοὺς ἐν φυλακῇ παρὰ τῷ δεσμοφύλακι εἰς τὸ δεσμωτήριον, εἰς τὸν τόπον, οὗ Ιωσηφ ἀπῆκτο ἐκεῖ.
hint: He puts them in custody in the prison where Joseph has been brought.

notes.text: Beside the gaoler. The Hebrew has bêt śar haṭṭabbāḥîm, the house of the captain of the guard, Potiphar's title at 39:1; the Greek names the gaoler instead.
The pluperfect passive of ἀπάγω, to lead away, carry off to prison: where Joseph had been led away, and still was. The relative adverb with ἐκεῖ, as at 39:20.
φυλακή, a watching or guarding, and also a ward or prison: in custody.

greek: καὶ συνέστησεν ὁ ἀρχιδεσμώτης τῷ Ιωσηφ αὐτούς, καὶ παρέστη αὐτοῖς· ἦσαν δὲ ἡμέρας ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ. —
hint: The chief jailer puts the two in Joseph's care, and they are held for some time.

notes.text: συνίστημι, to set together, bring together as friends, introduce, recommend: he put them in Joseph's charge. ἀρχιδεσμώτης, which LSJ files under ἀρχιδεσμοφύλαξ, citing this verse, is the chief gaoler of 39:21; the Hebrew has śar haṭṭabbāḥîm, the captain of the guard.
The second aorist of παρίστημι, intransitive: he stood by them, attended them.
The accusative of time: for days.
The printed page closes the verse with a dash, which the reading does not carry.

greek: καὶ εἶδον ἀμφότεροι ἐνύπνιον, ἑκάτερος ἐνύπνιον, ἐν μιᾷ νυκτὶ ὅρασις τοῦ ἐνυπνίου αὐτοῦ, ὁ ἀρχιοινοχόος καὶ ὁ ἀρχισιτοποιός, οἳ ἦσαν τῷ βασιλεῖ Αἰγύπτου, οἱ ὄντες ἐν τῷ δεσμωτηρίῳ.
hint: Both prisoners dream in one night, each a dream of his own.

notes.text: ὅρασις, seeing, a vision: each saw the vision of his dream. The Hebrew has kĕpitrôn ḥălōmô, according to the interpretation of his dream.
εἰμί with the dative of the one they belonged to, plain was, as at 12:20.
ἑκάτερος, each of two, in apposition to ἀμφότεροι: both saw, each his own.

greek: εἰσῆλθεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς Ιωσηφ τὸ πρωὶ καὶ εἶδεν αὐτούς, καὶ ἦσαν τεταραγμένοι.
hint: In the morning Joseph comes to them and sees that they are troubled.

notes.text: ἦσαν with the perfect passive participle of ταράσσω, to stir, trouble: they were in a troubled state, and remained so.

hint: Joseph asks Pharaoh's eunuchs why their faces are downcast today.

notes.text: Imperfect of ἐρωτάω, to ask: he was asking them.

σκυθρωπός, angry-looking, of sad countenance, sullen; no verb in the clause.

greek: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ἐνύπνιον εἴδομεν, καὶ ὁ συγκρίνων οὐκ ἔστιν αὐτό. εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς Ιωσηφ Οὐχὶ διὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ἡ διασάφησις αὐτῶν ἐστιν; διηγήσασθε οὖν μοι. —
hint: They say no one can interpret their dreams; Joseph answers that interpretation comes through God, and asks to hear them.

notes.text: συγκρίνω in Middle Liddell is to compound, compare, measure; LSJ adds to interpret dreams, citing this verse. The noun σύγκρισις follows it in 40:12 and 40:18.

διά with the genitive: is not the interpretation through God? The Hebrew has hălôʾ lēʾlōhîm pitrōnîm, are not interpretations God's?
εἶπαν, the aorist with the ending -αν, and εἴδομεν, we saw: one dream named for both.
The aorist middle imperative of διηγέομαι, to set out in detail.
The printed page closes the verse with a dash, which the reading does not carry.

greek: ἐν δὲ τῇ ἀμπέλῳ τρεῖς πυθμένες, καὶ αὐτὴ θάλλουσα ἀνενηνοχυῖα βλαστούς· πέπειροι οἱ βότρυες σταφυλῆς.
hint: The vine has three branches; it buds and its clusters ripen.

notes.text: πυθμήν, the hollow bottom or stand of a cup, the bottom or foundation, and of a tree the stock or root: the vine's three stocks.
Two participles of the vine: blooming, and having put up shoots. ἀνενηνοχυῖα is the perfect of ἀναφέρω, to bring or carry up.
No verb: ripe, the clusters of the grape.

hint: Joseph says the three branches are three days.

notes.text: σύγκρισις, in Middle Liddell a compounding, a comparing; LSJ gives interpretation, of dreams, citing this chapter.
The article stands with the numeral: the three stocks, those of the dream.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] to him [[name:Ιωσηφ]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[the compounding|the compounding, the comparing and comparison|σύγκρισις]] of it; the three [[hollow bottoms|hollow bottoms and stands of a cup, bottoms and depths, bottoms and foundations, anvil-stands, bottoms and stocks and roots of a tree, stems and stocks|πυθμήν]] three [[days|days, day-breaks, times|ἡμέρα]] are;

greek: ἔτι τρεῖς ἡμέραι καὶ μνησθήσεται Φαραω τῆς ἀρχῆς σου καὶ ἀποκαταστήσει σε ἐπὶ τὴν ἀρχιοινοχοΐαν σου, καὶ δώσεις τὸ ποτήριον Φαραω εἰς τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ κατὰ τὴν ἀρχήν σου τὴν προτέραν, ὡς ἦσθα οἰνοχοῶν.
hint: In three days Pharaoh will restore the cup-bearer to his office.

notes.text: μιμνήσκομαι with the genitive: Pharaoh will remember your office. The Hebrew has yiśśāʾ parʿōh ʾet-rōʾšekā, Pharaoh will lift up your head; the same Hebrew phrase returns at 40:19 and 40:20, and the Greek renders it otherwise each time.
ἀρχή, a beginning, and also power, a magistracy, an office: the chain carries both, and here the office is the cup-bearer's.
LSJ heads it ἀρχιοινοχοεία, office of chief cup-bearer, citing this verse.
ἦσθα, the imperfect of εἰμί, with the participle of οἰνοχοέω, to pour out wine for drinking: as you were, pouring wine.

greek: ἀλλὰ μνήσθητί μου διὰ σεαυτοῦ, ὅταν εὖ σοι γένηται, καὶ ποιήσεις ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔλεος καὶ μνησθήσῃ περὶ ἐμοῦ Φαραω καὶ ἐξάξεις με ἐκ τοῦ ὀχυρώματος τούτου·

διά with the genitive, through yourself. The Hebrew has ʾittĕkā, with you.
Φαραω does not decline; read as dative, you will make mention of me to Pharaoh, the sense Middle Liddell gives the verb last, to mention.

greek: ὅτι κλοπῇ ἐκλάπην ἐκ γῆς Εβραίων καὶ ὧδε οὐκ ἐποίησα οὐδέν, ἀλλʼ ἐνέβαλόν με εἰς τὸν λάκκον τοῦτον. —
hint: He says he was stolen from the land of the Hebrews and has done nothing to deserve the pit.

notes.text: A dative noun before its own verb, stolen with stealing, rendering the Hebrew infinitive absolute gunnōb gunnabtî, as βρώσει φάγῃ at 2:16. Middle Liddell gives the dative κλοπῇ as by stealth.

greek: καὶ εἶδεν ὁ ἀρχισιτοποιὸς ὅτι ὀρθῶς συνέκρινεν, καὶ εἶπεν τῷ Ιωσηφ Κἀγὼ εἶδον ἐνύπνιον καὶ ᾤμην τρία κανᾶ χονδριτῶν αἴρειν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς μου·
hint: Seeing the good interpretation, the chief baker tells his dream of three baskets on his head.

notes.text: συγκρίνω again, with ὀρθῶς, rightly: that he had interpreted well.
The imperfect of οἴομαι, to suppose, think: I thought I was carrying, the word of Joseph's own dream at 37:7.
κανοῦν, LSJ's κάνεον, a basket of reed or cane, a bread-basket; χονδρίτης, made of groats or coarse meal, of bread, LSJ citing this verse. The Hebrew sallê ḥōrî is of uncertain meaning.

reading: and [[saw|saw, perceived, beheld, looked at|ὁράω]] the chief baker [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[straight|straight, uprightly, rightly, truly and correctly, justly|ὀρθῶς]] [[compounded|compounded, compared, measured and estimated|συγκρίνω]], and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] to the [[name:Ιωσηφ]] and I [[I saw|I saw, I perceived, I beheld, I looked at|ὁράω]] [[a thing seen in sleep|a thing seen in sleep, a dream|ἐνύπνιον]] and [[I was supposing|I was supposing, I was thinking, I was deeming, I was imagining, I was expecting, I was fearing, I was foreboding, I was waiting for and looking for, I was believing|οἴομαι]] three [[baskets of reed or cane|baskets of reed or cane, bread-baskets|κανοῦν]] of made of groats or coarse meal [[to take up|to take up, to raise, to lift up, to bear and sustain, to raise up and exalt, to excite, to extol and exaggerate, to lift and take away and remove, to take off and kill|αἴρω]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of the head|of the head, of the life, of the top, of the brim, of the coping, of the source, of the crown and completion|κεφαλή]] of me;

greek: ἐν δὲ τῷ κανῷ τῷ ἐπάνω ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν γενῶν, ὧν ὁ βασιλεὺς Φαραω ἐσθίει, ἔργον σιτοποιοῦ, καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατήσθιεν αὐτὰ ἀπὸ τοῦ κανοῦ τοῦ ἐπάνω τῆς κεφαλῆς μου.
hint: In the top basket are baked goods for Pharaoh, and birds eat them from it.

notes.text: ἐπάνω, above, with the article as an adjective: the uppermost basket. At the end of the verse it takes the genitive, above my head.
γένος, race, kind: of all the kinds the king eats.
σιτοποιός is first an adjective, of grinding and baking; as a noun Middle Liddell gives one that ground the corn in the handmill, which heads the unit.
Imperfect of κατεσθίω, to eat up: the birds were eating them.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[in the basket of reed or cane|within, inside of, and by means of the basket of reed or cane, the bread-basket|ἐν; κανοῦν]] to the thing [[above|above and atop and on the upper side, above, above and more than|ἐπάνω]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single|πᾶς]] [[of the races|of the races, of the stocks and families, of the offspring and posterity, of the clans and houses, of the tribes and castes, of the breeds, of the ages and generations, of the sexes and genders, of the classes and sorts and kinds, of the genera|γένος]], of which [[the king|the king, the chief, the hereditary king, the lord and master and householder, the second of the nine archons, the king of Persia|βασιλεύς]] [[name:Φαραω]] [[eats|eats, eats of|ἐσθίω]], [[work|work, business, deeds, action, works of industry and tilled lands|ἔργον]] [[of one that ground the corn in the handmill|of one that ground the corn in the handmill, of grinding and baking, of a baking-woman|σιτοποιός]], and [[the winged fowl|the winged fowl, the birds, the able to fly and full fledged|πετεινόν]] [[of the heaven|of the heaven, of the vault, of the firmament and the sky|οὐρανός]] [[was eating up|was eating up, was devouring|κατεσθίω]] them [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of the basket of reed or cane|of the basket of reed or cane, of the bread-basket|κανοῦν]] of the thing [[above|above and atop and on the upper side, above, above and more than|ἐπάνω]] [[of the head|of the head, of the life, of the top, of the brim, of the coping, of the source, of the crown and completion|κεφαλή]] of me.

greek: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Ιωσηφ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Αὕτη ἡ σύγκρισις αὐτοῦ· τὰ τρία κανᾶ τρεῖς ἡμέραι εἰσίν·
hint: Joseph says the three baskets are three days.

notes.text: The article stands with the numeral: the three baskets, those of the dream.

reading: [[having given answer to|having given answer to, having replied, having answered, having answered charges and defended himself|ἀποκρίνομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ιωσηφ]] [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] to him [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[the compounding|the compounding, the comparing and comparison|σύγκρισις]] of it; the three [[baskets of reed or cane|baskets of reed or cane, bread-baskets|κανοῦν]] three [[days|days, day-breaks, times|ἡμέρα]] are;

greek: ἔτι τριῶν ἡμερῶν ἀφελεῖ Φαραω τὴν κεφαλήν σου ἀπὸ σοῦ καὶ κρεμάσει σε ἐπὶ ξύλου, καὶ φάγεται τὰ ὄρνεα τοῦ οὐρανοῦ τὰς σάρκας σου ἀπὸ σοῦ. —
hint: In three days Pharaoh will take off the baker's head and hang him, and birds will eat his flesh.

notes.text: The genitive of time within which: within three days more.

notes.lemma: ἀφελεῖ … τὴν κεφαλήν σου ἀπὸ σοῦ
notes.text: ἀφαιρέω, to take from, take off: Pharaoh will take your head from you. The Hebrew has yiśśāʾ parʿōh ʾet-rōʾšĕkā mēʿālêkā, will lift up your head from upon you, the phrase of 40:13.
κρεμάννυμι, to hang, with ἐπί and the genitive: on wood, on a tree.
The printed page closes the verse with a dash, which the reading does not carry.

reading: [[yet|yet, as yet, still, further, besides, moreover|ἔτι]] of three [[of days|of days, of day-breaks, of times|ἡμέρα]] [[will take from|will take from, will take away from, will take off, will remove, will separate and set aside|ἀφαιρέω]] [[name:Φαραω]] [[the head|the head, the life, the top, the brim, the coping, the source, the crown and completion|κεφαλή]] of you [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] of you and [[will hang|will hang, will hang up|κρεμάννυμι]] you [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of wood|of wood, of firewood, of timber, of a piece of wood, of a post, of a stick|ξύλον]], and [[will eat|will eat, will eat of|ἐσθίω]] [[the birds|the birds, the bird-market|ὄρνεον]] [[of the heaven|of the heaven, of the vault, of the firmament and the sky|οὐρανός]] [[the fleshes|the fleshes, the flesh, the muscles, the bodies, man's nature generally|σάρξ]] of you [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] of you.

greek: ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρα γενέσεως ἦν Φαραω, καὶ ἐποίει πότον πᾶσι τοῖς παισὶν αὐτοῦ. καὶ ἐμνήσθη τῆς ἀρχῆς τοῦ ἀρχιοινοχόου καὶ τῆς ἀρχῆς τοῦ ἀρχισιτοποιοῦ ἐν μέσῳ τῶν παίδων αὐτοῦ
hint: On the third day, Pharaoh's birthday, he holds a feast and remembers both prisoners.

notes.text: Φαραω does not decline; read as genitive, it was the day of Pharaoh's birth. γένεσις, origin, manner of birth.
Imperfect of ποιέω with πότος, a drinking-bout: he was holding a feast.
He remembered the office of each. The Hebrew has wayyiśśāʾ ʾet-rōʾš, he lifted up the head, the phrase of 40:13 and 40:19.
The printed page has no stop at the end of the verse; the sentence runs on into 40:21.

hint: He restores the cup-bearer, who puts the cup in Pharaoh's hand.

notes.text: No new subject named: the restored cup-bearer gave the cup.

hint: The chief baker is hanged, as Joseph had interpreted.

notes.text: The object first, with δέ against the cup-bearer of 40:21: but the baker he hanged.

greek: οὐκ ἐμνήσθη δὲ ὁ ἀρχιοινοχόος τοῦ Ιωσηφ, ἀλλὰ ἐπελάθετο αὐτοῦ.
hint: The chief cup-bearer does not remember Joseph but forgets him.

notes.text: ἐπιλανθάνομαι, to forget, Middle Liddell's one sense: plain text.
